title: boat-owner-is-read-not-stated
intention: cairn.devices.harbor_master.clearance.clear() obtains boat_owner from the BOAT rather than from its caller, so the Law 6 refusal cannot be satisfied by a caller choosing its own arguments.
why: The lived symptom, in the hands of whoever comes next: read cairn/devices/harbor_master/clearance.py and you are told the gate refuses an actor who is not the boat's owner and holds no grant — the sentence harbor_master's whole charter rests on. Then call it. Your call refuses; you change one string to match another string you also typed; your call passes. Nothing consulted the boat. A future device advancing a boat it has no business touching passes the same way, because it too will state both sides. The refusal is real code that runs and returns the answer its caller asked for.
traces_to: Law 6 (everything has exactly one owner; the owner alone gates writes — a check whose owner is supplied by the writer is not a gate)
Law 4 (a rule that matters is enforced by physics, not policy — a caller-satisfiable check is policy wearing physics' clothes)
Law 3 (nothing is known until measured — this was found by firing it, not by reading it; four readers had read past it)

falsifier.proves_green: code-seam@v2 gate-set, transcribed. PROVEME (non-skippable): proofs beside the code at cairn/devices/harbor_master/proofs/, run twice, sealed under the tester with isolation='netns' and persisted through validation_store.persist_validation. The Law 8 teeth: (i) a caller stating actor == boat_owner for a boat it does not own is REFUSED — the tooth that is GREEN TODAY on the reverted code, which is why non-hollowness here is proved by reverting and watching it PASS, the mirror of the usual direction and stated so nobody checks the wrong sign; (ii) the rightful owner still clears, so the read did not simply deny everyone; (iii) the read answers from files only — a tooth asserting no device, bus or network call is reachable from clear(). BUILD GATE: the PROVEME crossing runs build_inspector over cairn/devices/harbor_master at its own address. FEEDBACK TO ORIGIN ON FAILURE (Law 3+8 invariant): a red routes back to this ticket and to cairn/devices/harbor_master/intention+why.json, whose own falsifier is the sentence about devices advancing workflows around the rung — a failure here is evidence about that sentence.
falsifier.proves_red: DONE when cairn.devices.harbor_master.clearance.clear() obtains boat_owner from the BOAT rather than from its caller, and a tooth proves that a caller naming an actor with no standing over that boat is refused EVEN THOUGH it supplied a boat_owner equal to its own actor — verified non-hollow by reverting the read and watching the tooth go green (the reverted direction is green here, which is the tell: today's code passes that call). RED on any of: (1) the boat's owner ends up supplied by the caller under a new name — the same hole wearing a different field; (2) the read makes the gate reach outward at a crossing (a device roster, a live registry) — the chokepoint answers from files, and a registry is out of bounds by the parent ticket's own constrain; (3) every boat's owner resolves to the same string, which is the check being vacuous by a longer route. HORIZON: the first crossing made by an actor that is NOT the box's single hand — a second device, or Akien acting directly. Until such a crossing exists the refusal cannot be observed firing on anything real, and that is stated here rather than discovered later.

children: (a) where-a-boat-carries-its-owner — settle the ADDRESS the owner is read from. The ticket file is the obvious candidate because boat_id already IS the ticket id, but the ticket's existing `owner` field is prose about components in the wrong namespace, so this is a real design question and not a lookup. GATING: nothing can be read until there is somewhere to read it from, so this proves before the parent.

questions.a: One assumption was load-bearing and is now named: THAT THE AUTHORITY REFUSAL WAS DOING WORK. It is not. cairn/devices/harbor_master/clearance.py:1 compares `actor != boat_owner` and both values arrive from the SAME caller in the SAME call, so any caller can make them equal — including a caller with no standing at all. Measured 2026-08-10 during the first live fire of clear(): the very first production call refused as Unauthorized because the settlement had put boat_owner in the component namespace ('base'), and the fix that made it pass was to type a different string. A check a caller can satisfy by choosing its arguments is a declaration, not a refusal. Second assumption, examined and DISCHARGED: that the grant path rescues it — it does not, because Grant.authorizes() checks `by_owner == owner` where `owner` is again the caller-supplied boat_owner, so a caller who can state boat_owner can mint itself a grant from that same fictional owner.

One point I would have asserted wrapped and is not: WHERE the boat's owner is read FROM. The boat is the ticket (boat_id is the ticket id on every gated crossing), so the ticket file is the obvious address — but the ticket's existing `owner` field is PROSE about which COMPONENT owns which rung ('harbor_master owns the AUTHORITY rung; base owns THE DOOR'), which is exactly the namespace confusion this ticket exists to fix, one layer up. So the field cannot simply be read; either it gains a machine-readable sibling naming a MOVER, or the boat's owner lives somewhere else. That is a real open question and it is child (a) rather than smuggled past. Everything else is wrapped: the defect is measured, the mechanism is one comparison at one address, and the corrected settlement is already written beside it.

No exclusive-and-terminal collision; the congruency lab was recompiled and consulted 2026-08-10 before this cast, and boat_owner appears in exactly one intention — cairn/devices/harbor_master's own charter, which is this node's PARENT, not its rival. Two distinctions to record. (1) tickets/emit-refuses-an-uncleared-crossing (in flight, at WATCHME) landed the sixth seat and produced this finding on its first live fire; the whys are sequenced, not opposed: that ticket makes clearance MANDATORY at the door, this one makes the authority half of clearance MEAN something. Neither blocks the other — a mandatory gate whose Law 6 half is a declaration is still binding proven-space, resources and legality, which is three of its four refusals. (2) tickets/clearance-leaves-a-trace (cast 2026-07-26, at BUILDME) wants refusals recorded; that is about the gate's bookkeeping, this is about one refusal's content. Sequenced again, and in the useful direction: a trace would make this ticket's own horizon countable.

priority: P1 — P1 and not P0 because the gate it sits in is doing real work today: three of clearance's four refusals — proven-space, resources, legality — read from somewhere the caller does not write, and they are now binding on every crossing into a rest. What is vacuous is the fourth, and the failure it guards against (a device advancing a boat it does not own) has no live instance yet, because the box has one hand. It becomes P0 the day a second mover exists. It is not P2 because harbor_master's charter names this exact failure as its own falsification condition, and a component whose falsifier is met reads green while nothing derives red (Law 9).

It reports a finding on either of two conditions: (a) a cleared crossing landed whose boat_owner is not the value the boat itself carries — the read having been bypassed or drifted, which is the sharpest signal and needs no sample; (b) every cleared crossing since the era floor resolves to the SAME owner string, which is falsifier clause (3): the check vacuous by a longer route, indistinguishable from health without counting. Each finding carries the offending crossings verbatim with their component, seq, actor and resolved owner, so the consumer never re-derives them.

filed_edges: [CORPUS] A CHECK WHOSE BOTH SIDES COME FROM ONE CALLER IS A DECLARATION. This is worth a corpus-wide sweep and not only a fix here: the same shape is what makes a self-declared cleared_by dangerous (the parent ticket's falsifier clause (3)), what killed auto-inherit for chart claims (a door-minted value can never disagree with the door), and what the two-witness rule keeps re-deriving in different words. Somebody should count how many gates in this system compare two values that arrived together.
children_resolved: (a) where-a-boat-carries-its-owner — ANSWERED BY RULING, not by a child voyage. 2026-08-10-the-ticket-owns-the-refusal settled the address from above: the intentions own their tickets, a ticket owns its workflow, and the workflow IS the boat — so the owner is read from the TICKET, which is what `boat_id` has always been. The open question this child carried was real and the ruling dissolved it rather than resolving it: the ticket's `owner` field is indeed the wrong namespace, so the read does not use it. A NEW field, `owning_intention`, carries the address, declared in CairnCommons/tickets/_charter+why.json and distinguished from its two neighbours BY SHAPE — it resolves; they are prose. The child is therefore closed without being built, and closed by an authority above it. No separate ticket was cast for it, because there is nothing left to decide.
falsifier_sharpened: THE FALSIFIER ABOVE IS AMBIGUOUS ABOUT THE SIGN OF ITS OWN NON-HOLLOW CHECK, and it is ambiguous about exactly the thing it was written to pin. Its parenthesis — 'the reverted direction is green here, which is the tell' — is true of the TICKET-TIME tooth (a tooth asserting 'this exploit call succeeds' would be green on reverted code) but reads naturally as a claim about the BUILT tooth, which is the opposite. A later reader checking the wrong direction would find the wrong answer and believe it. The original wording stands (it is the evidence that this happens); the unambiguous statement, and the one actually run, is: THE EXPLOIT CALL — an actor with no standing naming ITSELF the owner of a boat it does not own — SUCCEEDS ON REVERTED CODE AND IS REFUSED ON BUILT CODE. Run both directions 2026-08-10. Reverted: the authority rung PASSED the call (it was stopped further along by proven-space, an unrelated gate, which is the rung under test letting it through). Built: Unauthorized, and no record written. The proof file itself does not survive the revert — it imports names the old module does not have — which is a second, cruder witness to the same thing.
assumptions_dispositioned: THE GRANT ASSUMPTION, named at cast and DISCHARGED by the build. At cast: `Grant.authorizes()` compared `by_owner == owner` where `owner` was the same caller-supplied `boat_owner`, so a caller who could state the owner could mint itself a grant from that fiction and the comparison would hold. Closing only the direct branch would have moved the hole one door along rather than shutting it. `mint_grant` now reads the boat too — it takes `minted_by`, resolves the boat's owner from disk, refuses a minter that owner does not admit, and stamps `by_owner` from the READ value rather than from anything the caller said. Tooth: test_a_grant_minted_from_an_owner_the_minter_invented_authorizes_nothing. A SECOND ASSUMPTION SURFACED DURING THE BUILD AND IS NAMED HERE RATHER THAN LEFT IN THE CHART: the decompose stage predicted that a cleared crossing would honestly record `delegated: true` always. It would not. cairn/tools/base/transitions.py:749 reads that field to render '(delegated)' on the crossing's standing line, so a constant there would mark every crossing delegated and inform nobody. The word keeps the distinction it has always drawn — a per-operation grant was spent — and the rejected reading is recorded inline at the emit call. That is a partial kill of hypothesis 6 and it is dispositioned as one in the verdict.
